text:
sophie: Quick sync — we need a decision on launch conditions for the multi-region + tenant isolation initiative. Sales surfaced 3 customers that need cross-region failover with P95 <= 120ms and strict data residency for EU tenants. What's the minimally shippable set we can promise by end of Q3? cc @mohit @lia
mohit: Can you paste the customer IDs and exact SLA language? We should separate latency SLAs from residency SLAs — the latter implies Private/VPC work.
lia: Agree. From a product POV minimal MVP = (1) region-affinity routing, (2) deterministic fallback to same-compatibility model in another region, (3) a canary & rollback policy. That avoids full tenant-sharding for day 1.
ryan: Ops caveat — cross-region fallback will kill KV-cache locality. Expect ~2-3x increase in cold-token latency for fallback hits if we don't do prefix caching replication. Need telemetry hooks for cold-warm delta.
jess: Cost note — naive cross-region failover will increase egress and GPU hours. Ballpark: +18-30% infra cost in worst-case failover. We can trade cost by restricting fallback to only critical routes.
sophie: Good flags. We need concrete launch acceptance criteria. Propose: "Minimum shippable" = routing policy + canary + automated rollback + docs + SLA playbook. Thoughts?
mohit: I like it. Add: measurable P95 for canary traffic (prod-like), and a signed customer expectation doc (no surprises). I can own the customer comms.
lia: I'll draft rollout playbook. Short checklist I'm thinking:
- canary at 5% traffic, region-affinity enabled
- automated fallback rules (region->nearest-compatible)
- telemetry: p95/p99 + cold-warm token latency + cache-miss rate
- cost-estimate + guardrail (max monthly egress delta)
- runbook + owner + escalation paths
(putting in the thread so we don't lose it)
ryan: Operational requirements from infra side:
- prewarm strategy for KV cache (warm-on-deploy + background prefetch)
- throttling & circuit-breaker on fallback paths
- trace sampling to link request->fallback->model-variant
I'll open infra ticket and link.
infra-bot: deploy-pipeline • canary-flag created: `canary/affinity-v1` — docs: https://internal.redwood/infradocs/canaries (auto-post) :white_check_mark:
sophie: Perfect. Can we list the gating metrics that must be green before we scale beyond 5%? I propose: P95 <= 135ms (canary) AND fallback error rate < 0.5% AND cost delta within guardrail.
jess: Add cost delta threshold: <= 12% month-over-month for customers on hosted plans, else require Dedicated pricing.
mohit: I'll formalize SLA wording and work with sales to lock expectations. Assign owner: mohit (SLA comms), lia (rollout playbook), ryan (infra runbook), jess (cost model).
lia: I'll attach a draft playbook by EOD.
sophie: Thanks — once playbook + infra ticket + SLA doc are in place, we get executive signoff and schedule a canary window. :thumbsup:
ryan: Created infra ticket #3456 and linked canary flag. Will post runbook PR once prewarm experiment finishes.
jess: I'll add a slide to next investor/product sync with cost/benefit summary.
lia: One more note — for customers that mandate EU residency we must gate any cross-region fallback that moves data out of region. That means for some tenants fallback = disabled and we need a separate isolation lane.
sophie: Noted. We'll include that as a hard gating rule (no out-of-region fallback for residency-constrained tenants).
mohit: OK — next steps: SLA doc + playbook + infra ticket updates. Can we reconvene Tue to sign off?
sophie: Tue works. Thanks all.
